findings.summary: Checked Sibley §sibley-1862-02-22 ('amounted to near 6,000 men') against OK004 Blunt ('which was near 7,000 men', already one_sided_bound upper). Adopted the reading near = nearly (a one-sided bound, tier-2 §3 item 4) so that both are coded the same way. NM001 us-sibley-6000 now has codes [adversary_or_hearsay_estimate, one_sided_bound] and bound upper. US stays C 2,500; the range changes from 1,750-6,000 to 1,750-3,500. OK004 is unchanged. The same reading is needed across batches (see A1).

Checked NPS (reinforcements arrived on the 27th; 'swelled ... to about 1,100' / 'about 900'), Scurry §scurry-1862-03-31 (1,400 in the March 28 fight) and Slough §slough-1862-03-29/-30 (1,000; 1,200 or 1,300; 1,200 to 3,400, all for the 28th). Each figure is limited to the March 27-28 phase of the 03-26 to 03-28 interval, as the March 26 figures are already limited to their day. Applied the table as proposed: us-scurry-1400, cs-nps-1100, cs-slough-1000, cs-slough-1200 and cs-slough-range get partial_interval, post_engagement_state and bound lower; us-nps-900 gets post_engagement_state. US goes from C 1,050 (900-1,400) to D, and Confederate from C 1,100 (770-2,300) to D. Wrote null_reasons, and the row is no longer counted as post_start excluded.

The GA001 reported-force-scope claim has phase 'unresolved', not post_outcome, so post_outcome_claim does not apply. Gillmore's 385 is the garrison 'found' at the surrender on April 11, after the frozen start of April 10. cs-gillmore-385 now has codes [post_engagement_state] and is class C, no longer unusable. The estimate is unchanged at B 390 (330-700).

Irwin's §baton-rouge passage relays Breckinridge's 3,600 and 3,000 alongside the figure, and its 'about 2,600, without counting the partisan rangers and militia' restates Breckinridge's 'did not carry into the action more than 2,600 ... does not include some 200 Partisan Rangers ... nor about the same number of militia'. Added reproduction_of 'cs-bk-2600' to cs-irwin-2600. Confederate goes from A 2,600 (2,470-2,600, reported_engaged) to A 3,000 (2,850-3,780, reported_effective), gaining applicability_unresolved and losing single_input.

Page image livermore-p79.jpg shows the source line 'c 8 W. R., 285' for Van Dorn's 14,000, and the loss line uses the same note. Van Dorn's p.285 (AR001 citation 10) reads 'The force with which I went into action was less than 14,000 men' and also gives about 600 killed and wounded and 200 prisoners, which match Livermore's loss line. Added reproduction_of 'cs-vd-14000' to cs-lv and extended the Livermore inventory reason with both source lines. Confederate goes from B 14,000 (11,900-25,000) to C 16,000 (11,200-25,000), basis unknown.

Page image livermore-p95.jpg shows the source line 'c 32 W. R., 140' for the Confederate 10,000. Hindman's p.140 (AR005 citation 6) reads 'less than 10,000 men of all arms'. Added reproduction_of 'cs-hind-lt10000' to cs-lv and updated the inventory reason. Confederate goes from B 10,000 (8,500-10,000) to D, with a null_reason. US stays B 10,000 (8,500-11,500) and loses basis_mixed. The row leaves set2_AB and set3_ABC.

Mouton §mouton-1862-11-04: 'at the close of the day ... my own barely reached 1,000'. The day is the fight day, the frozen single date 1862-10-27 (the narrative dates Faries's battery as 'ordered up' on the 27th and arriving on the 28th). A same-day state is not post_engagement_state; it is part of the interval. cs-mouton-1000 now has codes [partial_interval] and bound lower. us-mouton-close now has codes [adversary_or_hearsay_estimate, partial_scope, partial_interval]. The estimates are unchanged.

The 'near N' figures outside this batch (FL005 us-seymour, MO010 cs-prentiss-900, NC020 us-johnston-44000) are not in b2's file. Batch b2 now applies 'near' = 'nearly' = one-sided bound (R1, OK004). The primary should apply the same reading in the owning batches.

post_outcome_claim is used outside this batch on claims with phase 'unresolved' (AR009 cs-after, GA028 cs-hazen-garrison, KY011 us-morgan-hobson, LA010 cs-prisoners). These are not in b2's file. The primary should check them against R3's reading: post_outcome_claim needs a post_outcome-tagged claim; a surrender or after-action count is post_engagement_state or loss_timing not_prior.

Britton's 'not less than three thousand ... seven hundred and forty men' equals Foster's figures, but the passage does not attribute it to Foster. Under the v1 policy, a secondary figure is an opponent estimate only when the passage visibly shows it. The judgment call stays recorded in the input note, and the estimate is unchanged.

The FL003 rationale now says the frozen 1,573 'equals' Brannan's printed total, and the LA005 rationale says 1,392 'equals' Mouton's return total. Both add 'not linked: equal value alone'. No links were added, and the estimates are unchanged.
The MO014 and MO017 frozen numeric bounds that equal the casualty figures are already noted on us-cw. Both are kept as inputs and stay visible.
cs-slough-range's note now says the OCR reading '1,200 to 3,400' is unverified. After R2 it no longer sets any value.

The NM001 NPS cells' disputed side assignment stays coded scope_unresolved; any row-4 code gives the same class. The Confederate bound_conflict with Sibley's 1,750 is a declared consequence (design B3).
MO016, MO015 and TX001 sit oddly against their inputs because of how the engine works, not because of coding errors. Rationales and labels already show this.

Added one-line inventory reasons for NM001 citation 8's '1,200 of whom were old regulars', SC002 citation 4's components 3232/4313/1927, LA003 citation 14's '400 or 500 more' and LA003 citation 16's '3,200'. All are parts or earlier states, and none is entered.
The AR002 completed sum of Hindman's 79 + 35 stays at grade C. It is recorded as a judgment call in the S() note.
